cards.title: Why does a torch app want your contacts?
cards.body:
When you install an app, it may ask to use parts of your phone: the **camera**, **microphone**, **location**, **contacts** or **photos**. Each one is an [[app permission]].

A torch app needs the light. It doesn't need your contacts. Knowing what to allow is a quick way to protect your privacy.

cards.title: Only what it needs
cards.body:
- Allow what the app needs for **its job**: a map needs location; a video call needs the camera and microphone.
- Pick **"Only while using the app"** when it's offered, instead of "Always".
- You can change your mind any time in **Settings**.
- Many phones show a small **dot or icon** when the camera or microphone is on. If it appears and you're not using them, check which app it is.

Download apps only from the **official app store** on your device, and check who made them.

cards.prompt: Does the app **need** that permission for its job?
cards.explanation: Allow what fits the app's job: location for maps, the microphone for calls, photos for a photo editor. A torch, a calculator or a puzzle game doesn't need your contacts, location or microphone.
cards.hint: For each one, ask: could the app do its main job without it?
cards.nudge: Think about what each app is for. A permission that has nothing to do with that job isn't needed.

cards.prompt: You install a new drawing game.

steps.text: It asks: **"Allow access to your contacts?"** then **"Allow location: Always?"** What do you do?

choices.text: Allow both, so the game works
choices.consequence: A drawing game doesn't need your contacts or where you are, all the time.

choices.text: Say no to both, and see if the game still works
choices.consequence: It does. You can always change it later in Settings if a feature really needs it.

cards.explanation: Say no to permissions an app doesn't need. If an app **won't work at all** without permissions that have nothing to do with its job, choose a different app.
cards.hint: Would a drawing game need your contacts, or your location all the time?

cards.title: Public Wi-Fi
cards.body:
**Public Wi-Fi** at a café, library or airport is shared with strangers. Most websites use [[HTTPS|https]], so what you send to them is **encrypted** even on shared Wi-Fi.

The bigger risk is a **fake hotspot**: anyone can set up a network with a café's name. So:

- **Check the network's name** with staff before joining.
- For banking or anything important, use **mobile data** instead.
- Turn off **auto-join** for public networks.

cards.prompt: You're at a café. Which is the **riskiest** thing to do?

options.text: Join "Free Cafe WiFi 2" when staff don't know it
Read the news on the café's own network
options.nudge: Reading the news on the café's real network is low-risk. Look for the choice that could hand your details to a stranger.

options.text: Check your bank on mobile data
options.nudge: Mobile data is the safer choice for banking. Look for the choice with a network nobody can vouch for.

cards.explanation: A network the staff don't know about might be a **fake hotspot** set up by a stranger. The café's real network is fine for everyday browsing, and mobile data is best for banking.
cards.hint: The lesson said the biggest risk isn't the café's Wi-Fi itself. What is it?

cards.prompt: On a café's public Wi-Fi: fine, or better on mobile data?
cards.explanation: Everyday browsing is fine on public Wi-Fi. For banking or important accounts, **mobile data** is safer, because you can't always be sure a network is the real one.
cards.hint: Which activities involve your money or your most important accounts?
cards.nudge: Save banking and important account changes for mobile data. Videos, news and recipes are fine.

cards.prompt: What does **"Only while using the app"** mean for a location permission?

options.text: The app can see your location only while you're using it
The app sees your location just once, ever
options.nudge: That's a different option some phones offer. This one is about when the app is open.

options.text: The app sees your location all the time
options.nudge: That's what "Always" means. This choice is more limited.

cards.explanation: "Only while using the app" means the app gets your location while it's open and in use, not in the background. It's a good middle choice.
cards.hint: Read the words closely: while using the app.

cards.prompt: You're reading on your phone, and a **microphone dot** appears at the top of the screen.

steps.text: You're not on a call or recording anything. What do you do?

choices.text: Check which app is using the microphone, and switch its permission off
choices.consequence: Your phone shows which app it is. You turn its microphone permission off in Settings.
The dot means an app is listening right now. It's worth a quick check.

choices.text: Put tape over the screen dot
choices.consequence: The dot is only a signal. Covering it doesn't stop the app listening.

cards.explanation: The dot shows an app is using the **microphone**. Find out which app, and switch that permission off if it doesn't need it.
cards.hint: The lesson said what the dot means, and where you can change permissions.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Give apps only the **permissions they need** for their job. Choose **"Only while using the app"**.
- A **microphone or camera dot** you didn't expect? Check which app it is.
- On **public Wi-Fi**, check the network's name. Use **mobile data** for banking.

Next module: what to do when something goes wrong.
